summary: Instagram is doing the work: almost every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts barely moves except for a few videos. The best ones show a robot or a simple gadget doing something surprising, with a bold, funny or provocative title. Plain 'how does X work?' videos about doors, taps and alarms get far fewer views, likes, shares and saves.
winningPattern: Robots and hands-on maker gadgets (gyro robot, clap switch, line follower, mic vs speaker) with a surprising, personified claim in short Hindi-English (Hinglish) titles, e.g. 'X ke bina Y gir jaata', 'Z sunta hai, dekhta nahi'. They are posted mainly on Instagram, where they get 1,200-1,400 views and the most likes and saves. The few YouTube hits (500-700 views) share the same topics: gyro, clap switch, PIR sensor.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-module videos where something visibly reacts, falls or moves in the first 2 seconds
Write titles as a surprising contradiction: 'Yeh X karta nahi, phir bhi Y kaise?'
Post to Instagram first, since it reliably gets 10x the views, then cross-post to YouTube only the strongest ones
Reuse the proven topics (gyro, clap, PIR, line follower, mic) with new angles or sensors from the same family
End with a reason to save, such as a 'circuit cheat sheet' or 'try this at home' prompt, because saves are the clearest sign of interest
stopDoing: Stop making generic 'X kaise kaam karta hai?' videos on public-place gadgets (lift, mall door, taps, street light, smoke detector); several near-duplicate videos on the same topic split the audience
Stop posting English-only or flat explainer titles; the one English video got 161 YouTube views and 0 on Instagram
Stop using the repeated '🤔 Kaise...?' title template for every video, since the audience has stopped responding to it
